hints: Notice the upper plate is positive and the drop is negatively charged, so the electrical force pulling it upward balances its weight.
Recall the parallel-plate field is uniform with $E = V/d$ and the force on the drop is $F = qE$.
Check which changes alter $V$, $d$ or $q$, and which only alters the drop position where $E$ is still the same.
walkthrough: Identify the setup: a negative drop between horizontal plates with + on top and - below, held stationary so upward electrical force balances weight.
State the governing physics: the field is uniform with strength $E = V/d$ directed from + to -, and force magnitude is $F = qE$.
Apply to plate separation and voltage: smaller $d$ or larger $V$ makes $E$ larger, so $F$ becomes larger.
Apply to charge: larger magnitude of $q$ makes $F = qE$ larger for the same $E$.
Apply to position: in a uniform field $E$ is the same at all points between the plates, so moving closer to the positive plate leaves $E$ and $F$ unchanged. This is option D.

options.A: Decreasing plate separation $d$ increases field strength $E = V/d$, so $F = qE$ on the drop increases.
options.B: With $F = qE$, more charge $q$ on the drop gives a larger upward electrical force for the same field.
options.C: Increasing supply voltage $V$ increases $E = V/d$, so the upward force $F = qE$ increases.
options.D: The field between parallel plates is uniform, so moving position does not change $E$ and does not change $F = qE$.
